learning: Iteration 4 showed that 20 mm spacing helped the oval and s-bend, with line loss still at 1 per run. Span is the remaining sensing lever, so this run tests whether capture past the off-track limit removes line loss.
notes: Seven-sensor row spanning ±0.06 m at 20 mm spacing, lead 0.07 m. Controller matches iteration 4 except for weights scaled to about 33 times x, within the ±2 limit.
rationale: Iteration 4 is the best result so far (61.45). Its 20 mm spacing at lead 0.07 m raised the oval and s-bend and lifted the slalom to 47.8, but line_loss_events stayed at 1 per run, which fits the capture limit of the outer sensors at ±0.04 m. This iteration widens the row to seven sensors at 20 mm spacing, spanning ±0.06 m, all at y = 0.07 m. Outer sensors then capture to about 0.0785 m, past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Lead, footprint (12 mm), wheel radius, track, mass and body are unchanged, so the span is the only sensing change. The Builder suggested weights of 25 times x, but iteration 4 gave the best result at about 40 times x. I use about 33 times x, [2.0, 1.3, 0.7, 0, -0.7, -1.3, -2.0], which keeps the lateral signal gain between the two tested values and stays inside the ±2 weight limit. kp, kd, base_speed and last_direction are unchanged from iteration 4. Expected result: line_loss_events falling toward 0, max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, and slalom steering_oscillation at or below about 0.15. Risk: the outer sensors may dominate at large errors and raise slalom oscillation, in which case the outer weights should be reduced.
